A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MGE-LDM and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite relocated limitations and an added evaluation appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix E report original music-generation, source-imputation and extraction results, including architectural and sampling ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds COCOLA and CLAP-based evaluation results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The three-track latent representation, VAE/DiT architecture, velocity objective, adaptive timestep patterns, CLAP conditioning and generation/extraction procedures remain unchanged. Expanded explanations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use Slakh2100, MUSDB18 and MoisesDB with the same instrument coverage and generation, imputation and extraction tasks. The new metric evaluations reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: The reported extraction comparator changes from waveform Demucs to Hybrid Demucs (HDemucs), with a different cited architecture, revised implementation description and replacement scores in Table 3. MSDM, MSG-LD and AudioSep remain; newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix F substantially broadens generation evaluation beyond VGGish-based FAD/sub-FAD: it adds COCOLA for musical coherence and CLAP-based FAD/sub-FAD for total and partial generation, including ground-truth COCOLA references. Existing splits, sample counts, training budgets and inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The RePaint, normalization, CFG and generation-order analyses in Appendix E retain their settings and results, as do the qualitative examples. Appendix F adds benchmark measurements under alternative metrics without introducing a separate ablation, robustness test or error analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 9–11 add substantial COCOLA and CLAP-based result sets absent from v1. For SA bass imputation, T1 exceeds MSG-LD on COCOLA (60.93 versus 58.18), while MSG-LD has lower CLAP sub-FAD (0.071 versus 0.140). Table 3 also replaces Demucs scores with HDemucs scores, including SA bass 1.26 versus 1.49 for the different comparators. Existing MGE-LDM scores and ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The diffusion and conditional-score derivations in Appendices A–B remain substantively unchanged. The additional displayed perturbation equation restates existing mathematics; derivative-notation corrections do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: unified class-agnostic generation, imputation and extraction through joint latent modeling and adaptive timesteps, with heterogeneous-dataset training.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's modality-gap and data-scarcity caveats, v2 Section 6 proposes missing latent additivity constraints as a contributor to hallucinations and discusses possible remedies. Appendix F newly distinguishes musical coherence from timbral fidelity and explains metric-dependent findings. Earlier limitations are largely retained and relocated.

D1.justification: Appendix F specifies the CLAP checkpoint used for the additional FAD metrics and explains the COCOLA reference calculation; Appendix D.2 revises the baseline description to Hybrid Demucs. Most implementation details remain unchanged. The explicit promise to release code and pretrained models upon acceptance disappears, although the ethics statement retains a general release commitment.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted coverage of Diff-A-Riff and other accompaniment methods, latent autoregressive separation, discrete diffusion, evaluation metrics and Music2Latent. It also supplies the correct MusicGen-Stem reference where v1 cited StemGen. The central positioning against existing multi-source diffusion frameworks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language corrections, expands the method overview, moves limitations from Appendix F to Section 6, introduces the alternative-metrics appendix and adds acknowledgements. The main narrative and most paragraphs retain their original structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9–11 and revises table captions, rules and highlighting to distinguish overall winners from comparisons among SA-trained models. All four figures retain their image content; other layout changes mainly reflect text relocation and page reflow.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's VGGish-based generation evaluation, v2 adds useful evidence about musical coherence and alternative fidelity rankings, showing strengths of both MGE-LDM and its competitors. Clearer matched-training comparisons and expanded hallucination qualifications improve interpretation. These gains outweigh the limited loss of an explicit release-timing commitment and support an incremental overall improvement.
